title: The Gravity of Kepler Reach
premise: Silas Okonkwo, a clone who inherited both her original's debts and the unsolved murder of a dockmaster on Kepler Reach, pilots the long freight route between two colonies that severed contact decades ago. When the name 'Mara Okonkwo'—her original's name—appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew, Silas is pulled into a conspiracy: the colonies' ruling consortium has been quietly deciding which half of humanity's frozen sleepers will wake when Earth's final transmission loop ends. The murder was the first casualty of that vote. To survive, Silas must expose the manifest, unite the smugglers and dockworkers who became her found family, and choose whether to wake the half of humanity that includes her original's killers—or the half that includes everyone she loves.
about_author: Lior Pemberton is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard supply vessels before turning to fiction. Their work explores inherited identities and the quiet violence of bureaucratic power.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Silas Okonkwo runs cargo between Kepler Reach and Vesta Hollow, two colonies that stopped speaking after the Severance. In her POV we learn she is a clone of a murdered woman, living under inherited suspicion. She keeps her head down, logs honest hours, and avoids the consortium checkpoints. Emotional beat: weary isolation, the comfort of routine.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: At Kepler Reach customs, Silas discovers the freighter Perihelion—a ship decommissioned before her original's death—listed as active, carrying one passenger: Mara Okonkwo. Her own first name. Her POV tightens with dread; someone is baiting her. Emotional beat: the past reaching through paperwork to grab her throat.

chapters.title: What the Original Left
chapters.summary: Silas breaks into her original's sealed storage unit and finds encrypted logs about the cryo-vaults and a half-deleted message naming dockmaster Ede Yoruba—the murder victim—as an ally. POV shifts briefly to Ede's daughter, Nneka, who still blames 'the Okonkwo woman.' Emotional beat: grief and guilt braided together.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Smile
chapters.summary: Consortium auditor Dev Rask summons Silas, offering immunity from her original's case if she surrenders the storage unit's contents. His courtesy is a blade. Silas stalls, lying for the first time in her careful life. Emotional beat: the realization that invisibility was always permission they granted, not safety she earned.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Silas confides in her ragtag crew: engineer Tovi, ex-consortium medic Ash, and stowaway-turned-hand Juno. They argue about walking away; instead they commit. Found family solidifies over bad rations and worse jokes. Emotional beat: warmth as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: The crew locates the Perihelion derelict in a debris field. Aboard, they find cryo-pods—one occupied, its occupant biologically Mara Okonkwo, alive and forty years unaged. Silas faces her own face. Emotional beat: vertigo of selfhood; the clone confronting the original.

chapters.title: Waking Mara
chapters.summary: Against Ash's medical warnings, they wake Mara. She wakes swinging—paranoid, sharp, convinced the crew are consortium assets. Flashbacks reveal Mara discovered the Vault Protocol: a plan to wake only consortium-approved colonists when Earth's loop ends. Emotional beat: distrust between two versions of one soul.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Ash decodes Mara's data: Earth's transmission loop ends in eleven months, triggering automated vault releases keyed to a consortium whitelist. Half of humanity sleeps forever by design. POV widens via intercepted consortium broadcast. Emotional beat: cosmic dread made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: Nneka's Ledger
chapters.summary: Nneka Yoruba, now a dockworkers' union clerk, has spent years auditing her father's murder. Her POV reveals Ede died because he refused to falsify vault manifests. She confronts Silas with a weapon and leaves with an uneasy alliance instead. Emotional beat: hatred meeting evidence, and bending.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Zero
chapters.summary: Rask's forces board Silas's ship hunting Mara. A tense hide-and-seek through cargo bays; Juno takes a stun round covering the escape. Silas burns her clean record forever to get her people out. Emotional beat: the invisible life officially ends; family costs something real.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Saw
chapters.summary: Mara confesses her deepest failure: years ago she was offered a seat on the whitelist committee and refused so loudly they erased her—which is why her name on the new manifest means someone wants her silenced or framed. Rising tension: the conspiracy predates everything. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Parliament
chapters.summary: Silas convenes rival smugglers, union dockers, and black-market doctors at a neutral station. Old grudges flare; Nneka's evidence binds them. They form a loose pact to seize the vault control relay. Emotional beat: fractious coalition, fragile hope.

chapters.title: Rask's Offer, Again
chapters.summary: Rask privately offers Silas a place on the whitelist—for herself and her crew only—if she delivers Mara. He frames it as mercy. Silas nearly accepts; exhaustion makes survival seductive. Emotional beat: temptation, and the theme of power's corruption turned inward.

chapters.title: What Clones Owe
chapters.summary: Mara and Silas finally talk honestly—about inheritance, guilt, and whether a copy can owe the original's debts. Mara gives Silas her decryption keys, choosing trust. Emotional beat: reconciliation across the mirror; identity as choice, not origin.

chapters.title: The Relay Run
chapters.summary: The heist begins: the fleet scatters consortium patrols while Silas, Tovi, and Juno infiltrate the vault control relay. It goes wrong—Rask anticipated them, and the relay is a trap. Tovi is captured. Emotional beat: hubris checked; the cost of rebellion priced in people.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: In consortium custody, Tovi endures interrogation but leaks nothing; meanwhile Rask broadcasts Tovi's capture to fracture the alliance. Some smugglers defect. Nneka holds the union line. Emotional beat: endurance under pressure; loyalty tested publicly.

chapters.title: The Whitelist Leaks
chapters.summary: Ash cracks the whitelist using Mara's keys: the names include every conspirator's allies—and exclude entire station populations. They broadcast it colony-wide. Public fury erupts; the consortium's legitimacy cracks. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Kepler Burns Gently
chapters.summary: Uprising sweeps Kepler Reach. Dockworkers seize the yards; Nneka leads them past her father's old berth. Rask attempts to trigger early vault releases to destroy evidence—killing sleepers to save himself. Emotional beat: revolution's chaos, and the villain's logic laid bare.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Ship
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Silas and Mara fly the Perihelion itself—now repaired—on a suicide run to override the release sequence while Rask hunts them through the vault ring. They trade places mid-flight to spoof his targeting. Emotional beat: sisterhood as tactical genius.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Climax: the console offers Silas the same choice the consortium made—who wakes first, given limited power before the loop ends. She refuses the binary, burning the Perihelion's core to force all vaults open simultaneously, accepting the ship's destruction and near-certain death. Rask is arrested by his own security detail. Emotional beat: sacrifice breaking the arithmetic of power.

chapters.title: After the Loop Ends
chapters.summary: Vaults open across both colonies; millions wake to a changed world. Silas survives, burned and grounded, her pilot's license revoked pending hearings no one hurries to hold. Mara chooses to leave for Earth's silent ruins, taking the question of the original with her. Emotional beat: quiet aftermath, grief and gratitude entwined.

chapters.title: First Watch, New Route
chapters.summary: Resolution: months later, Silas runs a new route between colonies that speak again. Her crew—Tovi, Ash, Juno, and Nneka as union liaison—boards without being asked twice. A child born post-Severance asks why the ship is named Perihelion. Silas says it's the point where you're closest to the light. Emotional beat: found family enduring; survival justified at last.
